candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether merchant payments, flight attach, alternative accommodations, and connected-trip products keep increasing monetization without damaging supplier relationships or regulatory standing.
candidates.next_evidence: Pull latest 10-K/10-Q segment metrics: room nights, gross bookings, merchant vs agency mix, accommodation revenue share, payment-related revenue, marketing expense as a percent of bookings, and regulatory disclosures.
candidates.node_relation: Reference leader for the two-sided travel marketplace tollbooth model, with accommodation reservations, agency/merchant booking economics, payments, and connected-trip expansion.
candidates.theme_relation: Direct consumer travel beneficiary and context anchor for hotel supply aggregation, conversion at scale, and marketplace take-rate economics.
candidates.why_include: Use as the benchmark for what a scaled travel distribution tollbooth looks like: large accommodation reservation base, merchant and agency revenue streams, and supplier/consumer network effects.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included only as a reference anchor so smaller candidates can be compared against the best-known model.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether air and hotel distribution bookings stabilize or grow after the Hospitality Solutions divestiture, and whether Sabre Mosaic Marketplace improves supplier/buyer adoption and margin quality.
candidates.next_evidence: Verify 2026 quarterly distribution bookings, hotel distribution contribution, debt reduction after the $1.1B Hospitality Solutions sale, free cash flow, renewal activity with agencies/airlines, and customer concentration.
candidates.node_relation: B2B travel marketplace and distribution infrastructure connecting travel suppliers and travel buyers; hotel distribution remains relevant even after the Hospitality Solutions sale.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Travel distribution technology / global distribution systems
candidates.theme_relation: Second-order travel demand beneficiary whose revenue is tied to supplier transaction volumes rather than owning hotels, planes, or consumer-facing inventory.
candidates.why_include: Sabre sits one layer below consumer OTAs as travel distribution plumbing. Its public filings describe a B2B travel marketplace and transaction-volume-linked revenue, which maps directly to the tollbooth hypothesis.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Screens may classify it as legacy travel tech/GDS rather than a consumer travel marketplace tollbooth. The small market cap, post-asset-sale transition, and balance-sheet complexity can obscure the network-infrastructure angle.

candidates.company: Global Business Travel Group, Inc. / American Express Global Business Travel
candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether SME mix, supplier economics, CWT/Egencia integrations, and TTV growth translate into durable margin expansion rather than cyclically inflated post-pandemic travel recovery.
candidates.next_evidence: Check latest status of any strategic transaction or acquisition, 2026 TTV growth, client retention, SME penetration, supplier incentives, integration costs, leverage, and no-single-client concentration.
candidates.node_relation: Corporate travel marketplace connecting enterprise travelers with airlines, rail providers, hotels, car rentals, and other suppliers; acts as a demand aggregator and negotiated-access layer.
candidates.theme_relation: Second-order beneficiary of corporate travel recovery and managed-travel complexity, with supplier access, compliance, servicing, and software embedded into travel procurement workflows.
candidates.why_include: Its 2025 filing describes a marketplace connecting over 700 airlines, 160 rail providers, 1.3 million hotel properties, and other suppliers with business-travel clients, plus $36.3B of TTV and $2.72B revenue.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Often bucketed as business travel services rather than travel distribution infrastructure. Corporate travel is less visible than leisure OTAs, and enterprise procurement workflows create a different, less obvious tollbooth.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether paid membership increases lifetime value and repeat bookings without forcing uneconomic member acquisition or deteriorating supplier deal quality.
candidates.next_evidence: Verify paid member count, churn, acquisition cost, repeat purchase behavior, merchant payable risk, voucher/hotel inventory economics, direct supplier relationships, and dependency on third-party GDS/reservation systems.
candidates.node_relation: Niche travel-deal discovery and membership channel that can direct consumer demand toward travel suppliers and monetizes via advertising, vouchers, hotel inventory, and paid membership.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Travel deals media / membership travel marketplace
candidates.theme_relation: Speculative small-cap exposure to consumer travel conversion and supplier demand generation; potentially a narrow channel-access asset rather than a full travel marketplace tollbooth.
candidates.why_include: Despite sub-$300M size, Travelzoo has an unusual member/channel asset and is transitioning toward paid membership, which could create recurring revenue if travel-supplier deal flow and member engagement are durable.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Very small market cap, limited institutional capacity, smaller-reporting-company status, and classification as internet media/advertising can hide the travel distribution angle.

evidence.claim: Booking Holdings reported that merchant gross bookings increased year over year in 2025 primarily from accommodation reservation services and flight reservation services at Booking.com and Agoda.
As of June 9, 2026, web finance data showed Booking Holdings with an approximate market capitalization of $128.9B, supporting its use as a mega-cap reference rather than an underfollowed candidate.

Sabre describes its business as providing global travel solutions for suppliers and buyers through a B2B travel marketplace, with revenue largely tied to supplier transaction volumes rather than ticket or room unit pricing.

Sabre reported closing the sale of its Hospitality Solutions business for $1.1B in July 2025, while Q2 2025 distribution revenue was affected by air booking softness partly offset by increased hotel distribution bookings.
As of June 9, 2026, web finance data showed Sabre with an approximate market capitalization of $658M, fitting the small-cap underfollowed search lane.
Global Business Travel Group reported 2025 TTV of approximately $36.3B, revenue of $2.72B, net income of $111M, and adjusted EBITDA of $532M.
GBTG describes its marketplace as connecting travel suppliers including over 700 airlines, 160 rail providers, 1.3 million hotel properties, and other suppliers with business-travel clients.
As of June 9, 2026, web finance data showed GBTG with an approximate market capitalization of $4.86B, fitting the preferred small/mid-cap discovery range.

Travelzoo's 2025 Form 10-K indicates revenue drivers included paid membership fees and sales of pre-purchased vouchers or hotel inventory, and discloses reliance on third-party systems including GDS and central reservation systems for hotel booking services and travel package offerings.
As of June 9, 2026, web finance data showed Travelzoo with an approximate market capitalization of $110M, requiring below-$300M speculative-exception labeling.

MakeMyTrip's 2025 annual report describes dedicated supplier relationship teams and approximately 87,000 India properties, including alternative accommodations, available through its platform as of March 31, 2025.

As of June 9, 2026, web finance data showed MakeMyTrip with an approximate market capitalization of $4.43B, but it was not selected in the final four because the pass prioritized one reference anchor plus less obvious B2B/channel tollbooths.

memory_update.text: SABR should remain in the travel distribution tollbooth watchlist as a small-cap B2B distribution infrastructure candidate; next layer must test whether the post-Hospitality Solutions Sabre still has enough hotel-distribution and marketplace relevance.

GBTG is a mid-cap corporate travel marketplace candidate with strong supplier breadth evidence; later work must verify public-listing/strategic-transaction status and whether corporate travel TTV growth converts into durable free cash flow.

TZOO is a speculative shadow candidate due to sub-$300M market cap; keep only if paid membership metrics and supplier/channel economics show durable recurring value rather than promotional travel-media cyclicality.

MakeMyTrip has strong regional OTA and supplier-relationship evidence, but was excluded from the four-candidate cap; consider it in a separate regional OTA pass focused on India travel, hotel supply density, and regulatory/platform-power risk.

For this node, the highest-quality underfollowed search direction is one layer below leisure OTA leaders: B2B distribution systems, corporate travel marketplaces, hotel connectivity/channel management, supplier data, payments, and niche membership/channel assets.

node: Travel marketplace and hotel distribution tollbooths
summary: Expanded the universe around travel marketplace and distribution tollbooths with one mega-cap reference anchor and three underfollowed or lower-attention US-listed names. The strongest underfollowed exposures are not pure leisure OTAs alone, but B2B or regional marketplaces that aggregate supplier access, negotiated inventory, travel-management demand, airline/hotel distribution, and transaction data. Candidates require later-layer checks on take rate, supplier concentration, direct-vs-third-party demand, cancellation sensitivity, marketing efficiency, leverage, and whether public-market attention has already repriced the exposure.
